ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: In the circuit shown in the figure, what is the diode's operating state when it limits the amplitude?
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, the input end ui first passes through series resistor R to reach the upper output node; the right-side load RL is connected between the upper and lower bus lines of output end uo; D1 and D2 are also connected in parallel between the output node and the lower reference line, with opposite directions, forming a bidirectional limiting/clamping diode branch. Reasoning: The question asks the working state "when the diode limits amplitude." Limiting occurs when the output voltage tries to exceed a certain threshold; the parallel diode in the corresponding direction is forward-biased and conducts, clamping the output voltage within a range approximately equal to the diode forward voltage drop. Therefore, when the diode limits amplitude, it is in the forward conducting state.

raw_record.question_text: In the circuit shown in the figure, what is the diode's operating state when it limits the amplitude?

method.method_draft: First describe the image: identify R in series with the input and D1/D2 connected across the output/load as clamping elements. Then use the text phrase 'when the diode limits the amplitude' to infer that the relevant moment is clipping/clamping action. Apply the diode-limiter rule: clipping occurs when one of the shunt diodes becomes forward biased and conducts, holding the output near the diode forward voltage. Therefore the diode's operating state is forward conduction.

planner_metadata.distinctiveness_rationale: Directly uses the visual topology of the clipper/limiter circuit and the general diode clipping principle; this is the natural single reasoning route for this question.
planner_metadata.image_role: Read the figure as a limiter circuit: input u_i feeds a series resistor R, then the output node u_o is connected to load R_L and to two oppositely oriented diodes D1 and D2 in parallel/shunt across the output path.
planner_metadata.text_role: Use the question wording to focus on the diode state specifically during amplitude limiting, not during the small-signal non-limiting interval.
planner_metadata.knowledge_role: In a diode amplitude limiter, the diode limits/clips only after the applied voltage has biased it in the forward direction; in reverse bias it is essentially cut off and cannot clamp the node except by breakdown, which is not indicated here.
